site.metaTitle: Bibi – booking for meetings, food and the restaurant
site.metaDescription: One system for meetings and conferences, food and drink, and the restaurant's table bookings. For experience centres, museums, conference estates, manor houses and restaurants with private rooms. {amount} a month excl. VAT, {trialDays} days free.

hero.eyebrow: The booking system for venues without a hotel system
hero.heading: Meetings, food and the restaurant's tables. One system.
hero.lead: The conference in the Salon, lunch for the kitchen and tonight's table bookings share the same rooms, floor plans and lists. Book the whole room and its tables close, and the other way round. The money goes to your Fortnox or Visma.
hero.trialNote: {trialDays} days free, then {amount} a month excl. VAT. No sales call.

audience.label: Built for venues without a hotel system

jobs.title: The meeting, the food and the evening in the restaurant
jobs.lead: Often the conference runs in one system, the kitchen on paper and table booking in a third. In Bibi it is the same rooms, the same lists and the same team.

meetings.title: Create the order in one step
meetings.body: Add the room, food and activities at once, with no quote for smaller meetings. The order moves through your own statuses, the room is held soft or hard, and the customer pays by card, Swish or invoice through a link.

food.title: A run sheet the kitchen can trust
food.body: Needs are counted and matched to the dishes. The run sheet goes to whoever is responsible, such as the head chef, and every change makes a new version. Export it as pdf, csv or json when someone outside the system needs it.

restaurant.title: Run the evening on the floor plan
restaurant.body: Guests book their own tables, and staff see the whole room: who is arriving, who is seated and which tables are blocked. You set the sittings, which dates are open and which tables are kept for walk-ins. Tables join up for larger parties.

bookingPage.title: Guests book on your own page
bookingPage.lead: Each dining room gets a public booking page with your logo, your colour and your texts. The guest picks party size, day and time and gets a confirmation with a link to change or cancel.

manage.title: Change and cancel on their own
manage.body: With the link in the email the guest moves the booking or cancels it, up to the cut-off you set.

needs.title: Needs as counts
needs.body: The guest notes, say, one gluten free, from the lists you show to guests. No record of who eats what.

mail.title: Emails with your logo
mail.body: Confirmation, change, cancellation and a reminder the day before.

embed.title: On your own website
embed.body: Embed the booking page on your website, or let a partner site book through the API.

deposit.title: Deposits for larger parties
deposit.body: Ask for a deposit from a party size you choose. The guest pays on the same payment page as your conference customers.

shared.title: The same rooms, lists and money under everything
shared.lead: So nobody copies anything between systems, and nobody books the same room twice.

lists.title: Your own lists, counted
lists.body: You decide the lists: diets, allergens, accessibility or something entirely your own. The EU's 14 allergens come as a template. Needs are counted on orders and table bookings and reach the kitchen. No personal data about guests.

blocking.title: The room and its tables block each other
blocking.body: If someone tries to book the whole dining room on an evening with table bookings, Bibi says no. When the room is booked, its tables close to guests.

floorPlans.title: One floor plan, many layouts
floorPlans.body: Draw the room once. The same floor plan carries the conference's banquet layout and the restaurant's tables, combinations and tables that split.

setup.title: Your setup, not ours
setup.body: You set the types, fields, lists, statuses and responsibilities. Access follows three roles that you fine-tune per person.

assistant.title: Ask how the evening looks
assistant.lead: Ask how many covers there are tonight and which allergies the kitchen should know about, or have it book a table. The assistant works in Bibi as you, with your permissions, and nothing changes until you approve.
assistant.mcp: The same tools are an MCP server, so you can work in Bibi from your own Claude or other AI clients.

money.title: The money lands in your books
money.lead: Connect your own accounts. Fortnox or Visma raises and books every invoice and deposit, and card and Swish payments taken in Bibi are booked there.
money.note: One accounting system at a time. Bibi numbers nothing: every document shows your accounting system's number.

price.title: One price, out in the open
price.lead: No sales call and no quote. Get started, try it for {trialDays} days and pay when you want to continue.

facts.extraSeats: More seats at {seatAmount} a month each
facts.scope: Meetings, food and drink and the restaurant in one subscription

cta.body: Start a 14-day trial, add your rooms and invite your team.

following.name: Following
following.text: You follow it, someone else owns it

done.name: Past
done.text: The event has already taken place. The card is dimmed

blocked.name: Blocked
blocked.text: Red badge and dashed border: something blocks it, for example a double booking

fix.name: Needs fixing
fix.text: Amber badge and dashed border: something needs fixing, for example a preliminary booking about to expire

live.name: Live
live.text: Happening now. The card gets a green border with a light slowly running round it

assistantApproval.title: The assistant proposes, you decide
assistantApproval.text: Nothing changes until you approve. The proposal is only valid for a short time, and once it runs out you can ask the assistant to propose it again.

dashboard.title: How to read Workload
dashboard.body: Needs attention lists preliminary bookings that expire within 7 days, run sheets not yet sent for orders starting within 28 days and invoices past their due date. Utilisation is the share of the items' open hours that is booked in the period, and overlapping bookings count once. The order counts on the cards are neutral: more open orders is neither good nor bad.

forecast.title: Actual and projected
forecast.body: Confirmed bookings are accepted quotes not yet invoiced, by event month. The projection extends your average monthly invoicing over the past six months. Expected invoiced is the higher of the two, and the pipeline is the value of open orders, so it is not a promise.

hard.name: Solid
hard.text: Booked, the place is blocked for others

solid.name: Solid
solid.title: Booked: the place is blocked for others

outline.name: Outline
outline.title: Not booked: the place is free

search.title: Find what you need
search.body: Search by status, customer or place, and save a view you come back to often.

timeline.title: Your work, day by day
timeline.body: Every order you are involved in, grouped into Today, This week, Next week and Later. Open a card to go to its order.

toolbar.title: Choose the period
toolbar.body: Move through time, zoom, and filter which spaces you see.

grid.title: Bookings on a timeline
grid.body: Each row is a space. Solid bars are booked and block the space, striped ones are held and can be released, and a red mark means a clash. Click a booking to open its order, or click a free slot to start a new booking.

toolbar.title: Boards
toolbar.body: Switch between boards or create your own. The totals show what is on the board you are looking at.

board.title: Orders by phase
board.body: Each column is a phase. Drag an order to another column to move it. If the column holds several statuses, you choose which one.

status.title: Move the order along
status.body: Change the status here. Only the statuses allowed from the current one are listed, and some ask for a reason or an assignee first.

program.title: The program
program.body: The rooms, food and activities of the order, day by day. Add a line or a whole bundle, and see what is held or booked.

runSheets.title: Run sheets
runSheets.body: The run sheets for the kitchen and others are made from the program and its counted requirements, and sent from here.

details.title: Details and people
details.body: The type, budget and your own fields, who is responsible and who follows the order. The customer has a tab of its own.

money.title: Quotes and payments
money.body: Send quotes, ask for payment and follow what has been paid.

facts.title: Who it is for and when
facts.body: The order this run sheet belongs to and when it takes place. Open the order from here.

status.title: Status and sending
status.body: A run sheet starts as a draft. Publish it to send it to the responsibility, which can then mark it as done.

tasks.title: What to deliver
tasks.body: Every row to deliver, with when, what, where and how many. A star marks what changed since the last published version.

needs.title: What is needed
needs.body: The counted requirements, matched against your items.

versions.title: Versions and history
versions.body: When the order changes, a new version is made. Only the current version should be used. The older versions and what has happened to this one are listed here.

flow.title: Flow rules
flow.body: May move to lists the statuses an order can move to from here. If nothing is restricted, an order can move to any status. Gates show what an order needs to move into a status, such as a reason, an assignee or an accepted quote. Click a row to edit them.

grid.title: The status grid
grid.body: The rows are the order statuses and the columns are the item types. Each cell sets the reservation a line of that type gets when its order enters the status. Choose Keep to leave the lines as they are.

preset.title: The role
preset.body: The role gives a starting set of permissions. Everything below is measured from it.

grid.title: Allow or deny
grid.body: Allow or deny single permissions here, and they beat the role. Deny read on a feature and it disappears for the person. Changes save as you make them.

sections.title: What the sections do
sections.body: Each section you switch on adds a whole part to every item of this type: Pricing adds price and VAT, Availability makes the item bookable, Room layouts adds capacity per layout, Bundle lets it contain other items and Customisations adds option groups. You can add more later, but a section cannot be switched off while items have data in it.

build.title: How a run sheet is built
build.body: The types you pick give the rows and the fields give the columns. Lists count the requirements, and the responsibility receives the run sheet when it is published.

columns.title: Customize the board
columns.body: The columns are phases and the chips in a column are the statuses it shows. Drag chips and columns to move them. A status that is in no column is not shown on the board.
